bibl.title: Roman Ports on the Red Sea and their Contacts with Africa, Arabia and South Asia: Ancient Literacy and Recent Archaeological Evidence.
bibl.seg: Steven E. Sidebotham, Roman Ports on the Red Sea and their Contacts with Africa, Arabia and South Asia: Ancient Literacy and Recent Archaeological Evidence.
K.S. Mathew (ed.), Imperial Rome, Indian Ocean Regions and Muziris: New Perspectives on Maritime Trade (New Delhi, 2015) pp. 129-178.
bibl.note: Six sites at the northern end of the Red Sea have produced data, in some cases very modest, in other cases substantial, about the economic and cultural contacts with other areas of the Red Sea and Indian Ocean in the Hellenistic (323-30 BCE) and Roman periods (30 BCE-641 CE). A seventh site, thus far not located, but discussed by several ancient authors, is also worth mentioning. Examines both the ancient literary texts and also the archaeological evidence pertaining to these seven locales along the Red Sea shore.
